headword: {一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}

definitions.gloss: in a short time; overnight; in a day
definitions.explanation: A very brief period of time. Almost always used in negative constructions to mean something cannot be achieved quickly.

examples.japanese: ⟦{語学|ごがく}→語学：02770_gogaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{身|み}につかない→身につける：03158_minitsukeru⟧。
examples.english: Language skills can't be acquired overnight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{信頼|しんらい}→信頼：03268_shinrai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{築|きず}けない→築く：02046_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: Trust can't be built in a day.

examples.japanese: {一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{成功|せいこう}→成功：02638_seikou⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦わけ→わけ：01095_wake⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：noentry⟧。
examples.english: There's no way you can succeed overnight.

notes:
Literally "one morning, one evening" - meaning a single day.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Almost always used in negative sentences:
- ～は{一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}には～ない
- {一朝一夕|いっちょういっせき}で～できない

EMPHASIS:
The phrase emphasizes that worthwhile things require time and sustained effort to achieve.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧にして{成|な}らず: Rome wasn't built in a day
- ⟦{一夜|いちや}→一夜：08961_ichiya⟧にして: overnight (can be positive)
